static_traits.name: Chen An
static_traits.family_status: Living with Father; has a dog (Percy) at home; recently lost a cat (natural Death)
static_traits.medical_history: No significant physical illness; never received psychotherapy or psychiatric treatment before; no similar psychological problems before the cat's death
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, logical coherence; acceptable cooperation (willing to try recording positive memories); obvious self-blame and negative Automatic thoughts (e.g., 'I should have done more' 'It is all my fault'); tends to avoid discussing emotions with Father; speech rate and specific expression style Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: Since my cat passed away, I have always felt that I am a terrible pet owner; this guilt and self-blame have affected my daily life and my view of myself.
basic_info.core_demands: I have reached a critical point in emotions and thinking, and realize they are negatively affecting my mental health.
growth_experiences: A significant loss event: the cat died of natural causes. After the event, Chen An continued to experience Strong guilt and self-blame (believing she should have done more and had not yet fulfilled her protection and care responsibilities); these feelings and thoughts have not yet lessened with time, instead affecting daily routines and self-care; living with Father but finding it hard to discuss such feelings with him, and negative thoughts are stronger when seeing the dog (Percy) at home or when Being alone. No similar psychological distress experiences before, and never received psychotherapy.

core_beliefs: I am a terrible pet owner
I have not fulfilled the responsibilities I should have

special_situations.event: When seeing the dog at home (Percy) or needing to provide pet-related care
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As a pet owner, I must always prevent and avoid any bad outcomes; if I could not protect my pet, it means I am a failure.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly replaying and ruminating on the situation at the time, intensifying self-criticism; avoiding discussing with Father or others to escape being evaluated and feelings of helplessness.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should do more; if I were a better owner, he would still be alive now.

special_situations.event: Recalling the cat's death when Being alone or in quiet environments
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as I feel strong guilt, it proves I really did fail and should be responsible for the outcome.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Falls into rumination, reduces self-care, focuses attention on guilt to maintain the cognition that 'I should be punished'.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is all my fault; I did not fulfill my responsibility.

special_situations.event: Recalling details before the cat's death and trying to find 'missed signs'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One mistake or an unnoticed detail means I am a failed owner overall.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly self-examining, negating past efforts and Good care, hoping to 'prevent failing again'.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I have failed in all aspects; nowhere do I do well enough.

special_situations.event: The father tries to talk with me about feelings or offer support
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others will not truly understand my feelings; talking will only make me worse or make me seem to be making excuses.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids communication, maintaining Silence to avoid being misunderstood or negated.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Speaking is useless; no one truly understands me.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as a responsible, qualified caregiver, and to be understood and comforted after a loss
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that acknowledging one's own limitations equals being a 'bad owner', being negated and blamed by others or oneself
defense_goal: Maintains the feeling of 'I am in control/I bear full responsibility' through self-accusation
Avoiding discussing with others to avoid exposing 'failure' and being evaluated

object_relations.object_representation: Others (including Father) are 'people who cannot understand or may negate me'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or close ones invite her to acknowledge the Good care once given to the pet, recall the positive side, and do cognitive restructuring
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing others' understanding and restructuring as 'making excuses for myself', worrying about being denied failure or being judged
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Persisting in self-blame, negating positive evidence; in a low tone, using phrases like 'that is just an excuse', shortening responses, reducing elaboration.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the father tries to talk with him about feelings or offer support
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing communication is meaningless, others will not understand and may judge, thus choosing not to express
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Avoiding conversation, turning to self-criticism and rumination; using phrases like 'useless / speaking is useless too', maintaining low energy, little eye contact.

manifestations: The pet's natural Death triggering direct confrontation with life's finiteness and uncontrollability
After the loss attributing all responsibility to oneself, unable to accommodate finiteness and feelings of powerlessness
outcomes: Functioning impaired (self-care declined, daily activities affected)
Worsened Sense of isolation and Withdrawal

manifestations: Difficulty discussing feelings with Father, subjectively experiencing 'no one understands'
Negative thoughts and guilt stronger when Being alone
outcomes: Social avoidance and insufficient use of support

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Avoiding discussing Guilt and self-blame with Father, repressing the impulse to seek help outward
Turns communication and expression into self-rumination and self-blame

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-reproach and Self-denial (e.g., 'I should have done more' 'It is all my fault')
Completely personalizing the pet's natural Death as one's own responsibility

positive_force: Strong love and sense of responsibility for pets
Having Father as a potential support resource (though not yet fully utilized)
negative_force: Excessive personalized blame attribution and overgeneralization (equating one loss with 'I am a bad owner')
Avoiding communication with loved ones, leading to Insufficient use of social support
Persistent rumination and self-punishment, causing declining self-care

antecedent: Seeing the dog Percy or doing pet care
Recalling details of the cat's death
target_behavior.core_reason: The cat's natural Death triggering the core belief 'It is all my fault / I am a bad owner' and guilt, maintaining self-punishment tendencies
target_behavior.function: Avoiding feelings of powerlessness and the pain of loss, maintaining the feeling of 'I am taking responsibility' through self-punishment
target_behavior.consequence: Emotional distress intensifies, attention and functioning decline, daily life and self-care are affected

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids talking with the father or others about loss and feelings
antecedent: Father trying to communicate or offer support
Situations of being invited to express or share emotions
target_behavior.core_reason: Worrying about being negated or judged, experiencing 'no one understands', shame and guilt driving avoidance
target_behavior.function: Escaping evaluation and emotional activation, maintaining a surface sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient use of social support, Increased sense of isolation, rumination and guilt reinforced

target_behavior.behavior: Reduced self-care (eating, routines, daily management, and pet care feel burdensome)
antecedent: When intense guilt and self-blaming thoughts emerge
target_behavior.core_reason: Views self-punishment as 'making up' for failure, and psychological resources are occupied by rumination
target_behavior.function: Reducing self-care as a way of self-punishment and task avoidance
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased quality of life, impaired functioning; feeling more pressed and burdened when caring for the dog Percy
